raw:
I chose these hypotheses mainly on graph connectivity: whether an edit opens or closes the only path from input to output, or from an intermediate node to the output. I then checked each one against the 100 measurements. All ten are directionally supported by the experiments, but some rest on only one or two telling cases, noted in brackets.

1. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 3 helps more when edge 5 is none.** When node 2 has no route to the output, edge 3 becomes a much more important path. Evidence: experiment 72 gained +78 / +66 / +37. [Weaker: experiment 72 also has edge 4 = none, so the two conditions overlap.]
2. **Setting edge 3 to skip helps more when edge 3 was none.** Replacing a missing edge with a residual gains more than replacing an existing op. Evidence: experiments 31, 34 and 39 (from none) versus 32, 33 and 35 (from conv or pool).
3. **Removing edge 5 hurts more when edge 3 is none.** Without the direct path, edge 5 may be the main or only route to the output. Evidence: experiments 57, 58 and 60 versus 56 and 59.
4. **Removing edge 3 hurts more when edge 4 is none.** With edge 4 gone, deleting edge 3 can disconnect the output. Evidence: experiment 98 lost −74 / −57 / −26. [Weaker: experiment 98 also has edge 5 = none.]
5. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 3 helps more when edge 4 is skip.** All-skip cells have no conv in them, so adding one gains a lot. Evidence: experiments 73 and 74 versus 71.
6. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 5 helps more when edge 4 is avg_pool.** Pool-only cells badly need a convolution. Evidence: experiments 79 and 80 gained +37 to +48 on CIFAR.
7. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 0 helps less when edge 4 is none.** Node 1's features then only reach the output indirectly through edge 2. Evidence: experiments 93 and 94 versus 91, 92, 95 and 96.
8. **Removing edge 2 hurts more when edge 1 is none.** Node 2 would then lose all of its input. Evidence: experiments 88 and 90 versus 87 and 89.
9. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 1 helps less when edge 5 is none.** Node 2 then has no route to the output, so the new conv is mostly wasted. Evidence: pairs 62/61, 64/63 and 66/65.
10. **Adding conv3x3 on edge 4 helps less when edge 0 is none.** Node 1 then only carries a zero tensor, so the new edge adds little. Evidence: experiments 1 and 4 versus 2, 3 and 5. [Weaker: experiment 6 versus 7 is mixed.]
